model: RFM-LR1 (LoRaWAN module for the GSD8-RFM water meter)
frame: 2-byte header (Type, Index) followed by data whose width is fixed per Index. Type is 0x01 Set / 0x02 Query / 0x03 Action on downlink. No length byte, no error byte, no Device Type byte — nothing at all in common with this vendor's own IWM line, and byte 0x0A means CPU temperature here and 'reset the microcontroller' there.

set_status.description: 0x01 0x20 — write the alarm status byte. The written value is a mask of alarms to KEEP: 0x00 clears all, 0xFF clears none, 0x80 clears all but 'module removed'.

set_reporting_interval.description: 0x01 0x22 — reporting interval in minutes, 1 to 10080 (7 days).

set_starting_value.description: 0x01 0x25 — the meter's starting volume in litres. Intended for the ~2-minute CONFIGURE window after join; the meter should not be in use during calibration.

set_q3_max_flow.description: 0x01 0x2B — Q3 max flow in litres per hour, matching the mechanical meter's rating.

set_leak_window_size.description: 0x01 0x2C — leak detection window, in 15-second sample counts, 1 to 255.

set_leak_zero_tolerance.description: 0x01 0x2D — max opto phase changes still considered 'not moving', 0 to 255.

query_fw_build_hash.description: 0x02 0x03 — the firmware build hash (6 x Uint8).

query_cpu_temperature.description: 0x02 0x0A — CPU temperature, 0.01 C per LSB with a 50 C offset. Note that 0x0A on this vendor's IWM line is RESET.

query_reporting_interval.description: 0x02 0x22 — the configured reporting interval in minutes.

query_starting_value.description: 0x02 0x25 — the configured starting volume in litres.

reset_device.description: 0x03 0x05 — remote reset. The device re-joins with ALL SETTINGS BACK TO FACTORY DEFAULT and answers nothing.

telemetry_note: No telemetry decoder yet, and not because the format is unknown — it is fully documented. A single RFM uplink may carry several Type|Index|Data triples back to back with no length byte ('012100001738012008' is Volume plus Status), and the declarative field spec addresses fixed offsets. Decoding this needs a length-per-index loop, which is a codec shape this engine does not have. Recorded here rather than half-declared: a spec that read only the first frame would silently drop the second.

response.note: Type 0x01 is 'Data' on the uplink and 0x02 is 'Command NACK' — the only real negative acknowledgement in either B METERS family. KNOWN AMBIGUITY: the unsolicited status and volume reports (indexes 0x20 and 0x21) are byte-identical in shape to the echo of a Set on the same index, and the manual offers nothing to tell them apart. A periodic status uplink will therefore close an outstanding set_status. That is the best available answer rather than a defect to hide — the echoed value IS the device's current status — but it means a set on 0x20 or 0x21 is confirmed by the next report even if the device never applied it.

acknowledgement.note: A successful Set is echoed byte-for-byte as 0x01 <Index> <the written data>, so a write can be verified end to end. A refusal comes back as 0x02 <Index>. Correlation is by Index; there is no correlation id.

receive_window.post_join_note: The CONFIGURE window is ~2 minutes after join, with at least five uplinks at increasing 15s-to-2min intervals. It is the intended window for set_starting_value.
receive_window.operational_interval_note: 4 hours by default, settable over the air via set_reporting_interval (1 minute to 7 days). A queued downlink waits up to one interval.
receive_window.rejoin_note: The device re-joins if it hears nothing from the network for 288 uplinks (~36 days), so a network server that never sends downlinks causes periodic re-joins.
